title: Emergency Lane-Change Simulation: A Behavior-Guided Approach for Safety-Critical Scenario Generation

control_signal.value: No user-specified signal stated. The attacking vehicle is steered toward collision with the ego vehicle by a reward given when a dangerous scenario is generated, plus a GAN-generated reference lane-change trajectory.

control_mechanism.value: Recurrent PPO policy for the attack vehicle, guided by the reference trajectory from the behavior learning module (GA-SeqGAN); model predictive control applies physical constraints to the reference trajectory.

base_model.value: GA-SeqGAN (SeqGAN with GRU generator and attention layer) for behavior learning; RecurrentPPO attack policy; MPC; validated in the CARLA simulator.

datasets.value: HighD drone highway dataset; 520 extracted emergency lane-change trajectories (duration under 2 seconds).

metrics.value: Negative log-likelihood of generated sequences under real data distribution (NLLreal), TTC-based risk, collision success rate, training reward convergence, computation time against grid search, manual design, random sampling, and Learning to collision.

controllability_evidence.value: Across 100 trials, attack trajectories with behavior guidance align more closely with real data than without; the method converges faster than PPO, TD3, DDPG and beats baselines on collision success rate (numbers shown only in figures).

stated_limitations.value: Packet states future work only (testing against state-of-the-art AV driving algorithms, converting to video and radar data); the scenario scope is emergency lane changes on highway or expressway.

notes: Reward/RL-driven adversarial attack with GAN reference trajectory; family 'other' is a judgement call (not tilting, not guidance). No explicit limitations section in the packet.
